question_text: During a Part 107 operation, may a visual observer (VO) assume control of the small unmanned aircraft during flight?

options.text: Yes, at any time, if the remote pilot in command authorizes it
Yes, but only in an emergency situation
No, a visual observer may not manipulate the flight controls

explanation_correct: Answer sourced from FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide.

question_text: In small unmanned aircraft operations, what best describes the control station?

options.text: The physical location where the remote pilot stands while monitoring the flight
The ground-based control equipment used by the remote pilot to operate the small unmanned aircraft at the pilot's location
The launch and recovery area designated for the sUAS operation

explanation_correct: Answer sourced from FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide.

question_text: Which statement is correct regarding a small UAS operation during an in-flight emergency?

options.text: The remote pilot in command must immediately terminate the flight, regardless of surrounding hazards.
The remote pilot in command may deviate from Part 107 rules to avoid collision with a manned aircraft.
The remote pilot in command must get ATC approval before deviating from a rule.

explanation_correct: Answer sourced from FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide.

question_text: You purchased an older drone that does not have Standard Remote ID and weighs more than 250 grams. What is required to legally fly the drone in Class G airspace?

options.text: A Remote ID broadcast module
Authorization from the FAA
An internet connection to transmit Remote ID data

question_text: If you are planning to fly your small unmanned aircraft and the cloud ceiling is 600 feet AGL, what is the maximum altitude you may legally fly?

options.text: 400 feet AGL
500 feet AGL
100 feet AGL

explanation_correct: Answer sourced from FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide.

question_text: When may a remote pilot operate a small unmanned aircraft during civil twilight?

options.text: With anti-collision lights visible for 3 SM
With anti-collision lights visible for at least 3 SM and flashing
With anti-collision lights flashing and visible for 1 statute mile

question_text: A remote pilot is conducting a small unmanned aircraft operation over open farmland. A visual observer (VO) is assisting the remote pilot by tracking the aircraft using binoculars to maintain visual line of sight. Is this operation compliant with Part 107?

options.text: Yes, a visual observer may use binoculars to maintain visual line of sight
Yes, as long as the remote pilot can see the aircraft at all times
No, a visual observer must maintain visual line of sight using unaided vision

explanation_correct: Answer sourced from FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide.

question_text: A visual observer (VO) sees a manned aircraft approaching the small unmanned aircraft but fails to notify the remote pilot in command (RPIC). What is the RPIC's responsibility in this situation?

options.text: The RPIC is still responsible for avoiding the manned aircraft and must take immediate action
The VO's failure relieves the RPIC of responsibility
The RPIC may continue the operation since the VO saw the aircraft

explanation_correct: Answer sourced from FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide.

question_text: After the preflight briefing, the remote pilot in command (RPIC) realizes they forgot to inform the crew that the small unmanned aircraft will not use obstacle avoidance systems due to the nature of the operation. What should the RPIC do?

options.text: Proceed with the operation since the crew is already briefed
Stop and update the briefing to ensure the crew understands the limitation
Rely on the crew to notice obstacles and adjust accordingly

explanation_correct: Answer sourced from FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide.

question_text: For Part 107 operations, civil twilight is defined as which of the following time periods?

options.text: When the sun is between 0 degrees and 6 degrees below the horizon
30 minutes before sunrise and 30 minutes after sunset
Any time the sky is partially illuminated

question_text: Who is responsible for ensuring a small UAS is properly equipped for night or civil twilight operations?

options.text: The aircraft manufacturer
Air traffic control
The remote pilot in command

question_text: Under 14 CFR Sec. 89.130, what must an operator of a foreign-registered unmanned aircraft do before operating in U.S. airspace?

options.text: Register the aircraft with the FAA under Part 48
Obtain a Confirmation of Identification and keep it at the control station
Display the aircraft's registration number on the exterior
